verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle not from men, nor through a man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him up from the dead,
verses.1:2: and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia.
verses.1:3: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:4: who gave Himself for our sins, so that He might rescue us from the present wicked age, according to the will of our God and Father,
verses.1:5: to whom belongs glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:6: I am amazed that you are so very quickly turning away from Him who called you into the grace of Christ to another gospel,
verses.1:7: which is not another, except that there are some who are disturbing you and want to overturn the gospel of Christ.
verses.1:8: But even if we or an angel from heaven should proclaim a gospel to you other than what we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.
verses.1:9: Just as we said before, now I also say again: if anyone proclaims a gospel to you other than what you received, let him be accursed.
verses.1:10: For am I now trying to persuade men, or God? Or am I seeking to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
verses.1:11: For I make known to you, brothers, that the gospel which was proclaimed by me is not according to man;
verses.1:12: for I myself neither received it from a man nor learned it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:13: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism: how beyond measure I was persecuting the church of God and trying to overthrow it,
verses.1:14: and I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my own people, being more exceedingly zealous for my ancestral traditions.
verses.1:15: But when it pleased Him who separated me from my mother's womb and called me through His grace,
verses.1:16: to reveal His Son in me, so that I might proclaim Him among the Gentiles, immediately I did not consent to flesh and blood,
verses.1:17: nor did I go to Jerusalem to my predecessors, the apostles; but I went away into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.
verses.1:18: Then after three years I went to Jerusalem to see Peter, and I stayed with him for fifteen days;
verses.1:19: but I saw no other of the apostles, except James, the brother of the Lord.
verses.1:20: Now the things that I am writing to you—look, before God, I am not lying.
verses.1:21: Afterward I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
verses.1:22: Now I was not known by face to the churches of Judea that were in Christ;
verses.1:23: they only had the report, "The one who once persecuted us is now proclaiming the faith that he once tried to overthrow";
verses.1:24: and in me they were glorifying God.
verses.2:1: Then, after fourteen years, I again went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas, having taken Titus along as well.
verses.2:2: Now I went up according to a revelation, and I laid before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles, yet privately to those who seemed to be something, for fear that I was somehow running, or had run, in vain.
verses.2:3: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, although he was a Gentile, was compelled to be circumcised;
verses.2:4: but because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy out our freedom which we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might reduce us to slavery.
verses.2:5: Not even for an hour did we give way to them in submission, so that the truth of the gospel may remain with you.
verses.2:6: Now from those who seemed to be something (whatever sort they once were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality toward any man)—for those who seemed to be something contributed nothing to me.
verses.2:7: But on the contrary, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision had been entrusted to me, just as that of the circumcision was to Peter
verses.2:8: (for He who worked for Peter toward the apostleship of the circumcision also worked for me among the Gentiles),
verses.2:9: and when they recognized the grace that had been given to me, James and Cephas and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision;
verses.2:10: only that we should remember the poor, which is the very thing I too was eager to do.
verses.2:11: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, because he was blameworthy.
verses.2:12: For before some men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they had come, he began to draw back and separate himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision.
verses.2:13: And the rest of the Jews consented to his hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was led by them into that hypocrisy.
verses.2:14: But when I saw that they were not walking rightly in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of everyone, "If you, though you are a Jew, live in the Gentile way and not in the Jewish way, how do you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?"
verses.2:15: We by nature are Jews, and not sinners from among the Gentiles.
verses.2:16: Yet knowing that a man is not justified by works of the law, except through the faith of Jesus Christ, we also believe in Christ Jesus, so that we may be justified by the faith of Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no flesh will be justified.
verses.2:17: But if, seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found to be sinners, is Christ a minister of sin? Far from it!
verses.2:18: For if I build up again those very things that I tore down, I establish myself as a transgressor.
verses.2:19: For I, through the law, died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been nailed to the cross with Christ.
verses.2:20: And I live—no longer I, but Christ lives in me. And what I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and handed Himself over for me.
verses.2:21: I do not cast aside the grace of God. For if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
verses.3:1: Unthinking Galatians, who has bewitched you not to obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was portrayed, crucified among you?
verses.3:2: This alone I want to learn from you: did you receive the Spirit from works of the law, or from the hearing of faith?
verses.3:3: Are you so foolish that, although you began by the Spirit, you are now being brought to completion by the flesh?
verses.3:4: Have you suffered such great things for nothing? If indeed for nothing.
verses.3:5: Therefore He who grants the Spirit to you and works mighty deeds among you: is it from works of the law, or from the hearing of faith?
verses.3:6: Just as it is written: "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness."
verses.3:7: Know, therefore, that those who are of faith, they are sons of Abraham.
verses.3:8: Now Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the nations by faith, announced beforehand to Abraham: "All the nations will be blessed in you."
verses.3:9: Therefore those who are of faith will be blessed with faithful Abraham.
verses.3:10: For all who are of works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: "Cursed is everyone who does not remain in all the things that are written in the book of the law, to do them."
verses.3:11: Now it is clear that no one is justified in the law before God, because the righteous one lives by faith.
verses.3:12: Yet the law is not of faith, but: "The one who does them will live in them."
verses.3:13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us, because it is written: "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree";
verses.3:14: so that among the nations the blessing of Abraham might come in Christ Jesus, so that we may receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
verses.3:15: Brothers (I speak in human terms), yet no one rejects or adds to a man's confirmed covenant.
verses.3:16: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, "And to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "And to your seed," who is Christ.
verses.3:17: Now this I say: the law, which came into being four hundred and thirty years later, does not make void a covenant confirmed by God, so as to abolish the promise.
verses.3:18: For if the inheritance is from the law, it is no longer from promise. Yet God granted it to Abraham through promise.
verses.3:19: Why then the law? It was set in place because of transgressions until the seed should come to whom He had promised, ordained through angels in the hand of a mediator.
verses.3:20: Now a mediator is not of one, yet God is one.
verses.3:21: Is the law therefore against the promises of God? Far from it! For if a law had been given that could give life, truly righteousness would be from the law.
verses.3:22: But Scripture confined all things under sin, so that the promise from the faith of Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
verses.3:23: Now before faith came, we were guarded under the law, confined for that faith which was to be revealed.
verses.3:24: Therefore the law was our custodian in Christ, so that we may be justified by faith.
verses.3:25: But when faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian.
verses.3:26: For you are all sons of God through the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:27: For all of you who were baptized in Christ have put on Christ.
verses.3:28: There is no Jew or Greek; there is no slave or free; there is no male or female. For all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:29: Now if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to promise.
verses.4:1: Now I say: as long as the heir is a young child, he differs in nothing from a slave, though he is lord of all,
verses.4:2: but is under guardians and stewards until the time appointed beforehand by the father;
verses.4:3: so we also, when we were young children, were serving as slaves under the elements of the world.
verses.4:4: But when the fullness of time arrived, God sent His Son, made from a woman, made under the law,
verses.4:5: so that He might redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive the adoption of sons.
verses.4:6: Now because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying out: "Abba, Father."
verses.4:7: Therefore he is no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, also an heir through God.
verses.4:8: Yet at that time indeed, not knowing God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
verses.4:9: But now, since you have come to know God, or rather have been known by God, how are you turning back again to the weak and needy elements, to which you want to be slaves once more?
verses.4:10: You observe days, and months, and seasons, and years.
verses.4:11: I fear for you, that perhaps I have labored among you for nothing.
verses.4:12: Be as I am, because I also am as you are; brothers, I implore you. You have not wronged me at all.
verses.4:13: Now you know that through weakness of the flesh I proclaimed the gospel to you previously, and your trial in my flesh
verses.4:14: you did not despise or reject, but you welcomed me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
verses.4:15: Where then is your blessedness? For I bear witness to you that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
verses.4:16: Have I therefore become an enemy to you by speaking the truth to you?
verses.4:17: They are zealous for you, not honorably; rather, they want to exclude you, so that you may be zealous for them.
verses.4:18: Yet be zealous for what is good in a good thing always, and not only when I am present with you.
verses.4:19: My little children, for whom I am in labor again until Christ is formed in you,
verses.4:20: I would indeed wish to be with you right now and to change my voice, because I am confounded about you.
verses.4:21: Tell me, you who want to be under the law: have you not read the law?
verses.4:22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: one from the slave woman, and one from the free woman.
verses.4:23: Yet the one from the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the one from the free woman was through promise,
verses.4:24: which things are spoken through allegory. For these are two covenants: one indeed on Mount Sinai, giving birth into slavery, which is Hagar.
verses.4:25: For Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, which is joined to the Jerusalem that is now, and is in slavery with her children.
verses.4:26: But that Jerusalem which is above is free, who is our mother.
verses.4:27: For it is written: "Rejoice, barren one, you who do not bear; break forth and cry out, you who are not in labor, because many are the children of the desolate woman, more than of her who has a husband."
verses.4:28: Now we, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.
verses.4:29: Yet just as at that time the one who had been born according to the flesh persecuted the one who was according to the Spirit, so also now.
verses.4:30: But what does Scripture say? "Drive out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman will not be an heir with the son of the free woman."
verses.4:31: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman, by the freedom with which Christ freed us.
verses.5:1: Stand firm, and do not be held fast again by a yoke of slavery.
verses.5:2: Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you are circumcised, Christ will not benefit you at all.
verses.5:3: Now I testify again to every man who circumcises himself that he is obligated to do the entire law.
verses.5:4: You have been separated from Christ, you who are justified in the law; you have fallen from grace.
verses.5:5: For by the Spirit, from faith, we await the hope of righteousness.
verses.5:6: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value, but faith that works through love.
verses.5:7: You were running well; who prevented you from obeying the truth?
verses.5:8: This persuasion does not come from Him who is calling you.
verses.5:9: A little leaven corrupts the entire lump.
verses.5:10: I am confident in you in the Lord that you will be of no other mind; but the one who unsettles you will bear the judgment, whoever he is.
verses.5:11: But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why do I still suffer persecution? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been nullified.
verses.5:12: I wish that those who unsettle you would even be cut off.
verses.5:13: For you were called to freedom, brothers; only do not give freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through the love of the Spirit serve one another.
verses.5:14: For the entire law is fulfilled in one statement: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.5:15: But if you bite and devour one another, see to it that you are not consumed by one another.
verses.5:16: Now I say: walk by the Spirit, and you will not accomplish the desires of the flesh.
verses.5:17: For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these oppose one another, so that whatever things you wish, you do not do them.
verses.5:18: Now if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
verses.5:19: Now the works of the flesh are plain, which are fornication, impurity, indecency, debauchery,
verses.5:20: slavery to idols, sorceries, enmities, contentions, jealousies, rages, quarrels, dissensions, sects,
verses.5:21: envies, murders, bouts of drunkenness, revelries, and things similar to these, about which I am forewarning you, just as I forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not obtain the kingdom of God.
verses.5:22: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, forbearance,
verses.5:23: meekness, faith, modesty, self-control, chastity. Against things of this kind there is no law.
verses.5:24: And those who belong to Christ have crucified their flesh with its vices and cravings.
verses.5:25: If by the Spirit we live, by the Spirit let us also walk.
verses.5:26: Let us not become eager for empty glory, provoking one another, envying one another.
verses.6:1: Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some offense, you who are spiritual, instruct such a one in a spirit of gentleness, examining yourself, so that you too may not be tempted.
verses.6:2: Bear one another's burdens, and thus you will fulfill the law of Christ.
verses.6:3: For if anyone considers himself to be something when he is nothing, he deludes himself.
verses.6:4: But let each one test his own work, and then he will have glory in himself alone, and not in another.
verses.6:5: For each one will bear his own burden.
verses.6:6: Now let the one who is taught in the word share with the one who teaches him in all good things.
verses.6:7: Do not be mistaken: God is not mocked.
verses.6:8: For whatever things a man sows, these he will also reap. For the one who sows in his own flesh will also reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows in the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
verses.6:9: And in doing good, let us not grow faint; for in its own time we will reap, if we do not grow faint.
verses.6:10: Therefore, while we have time, let us do good to all, but especially to those of the household of faith.
verses.6:11: See with what kind of letters I have written to you by my own hand.
verses.6:12: For all who want to please in the flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.
verses.6:13: For not even those who are circumcised keep the law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
verses.6:14: But may it be far from me to boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
verses.6:15: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value, but a new creation.
verses.6:16: And as for all who follow this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
verses.6:17: From now on, let no one trouble me, for I bear the brand marks of the Lord Jesus in my body.
verses.6:18: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

notes.1:6: The Vulgate reads in gratiam (accusative, "into the grace") rather than "in the grace," and uses the same word aliud ("another") in both verses 6 and 7, whereas the Greek distinguishes heteron ("different") and allo ("another").
notes.1:12: The Vulgate uses the active verb didici ("nor learned it"), whereas the Greek has the passive edidachthen ("nor was I taught it").
notes.1:16: The Vulgate translates the Greek "did not consult with" with non acquievi ("did not consent to" or "did not yield to").
notes.1:18: The Clementine Vulgate reads Petrum ("Peter") here and Petro in 2:7-8, while using Cephas in 2:9, 11, and 14; many critical Greek editions read "Cephas" here as well.
notes.2:3: The Vulgate reads gentilis ("a Gentile") where the Greek text has Hellen ("a Greek").
notes.2:13: The Vulgate reads duceretur ab eis in illam simulationem ("was led by them into that hypocrisy"), whereas the Greek has "was carried away by their hypocrisy."
notes.2:14: Commentators differ on whether Paul's spoken address to Cephas ends at verse 14 or continues through verse 21.
notes.2:16: Latin fidem Jesu Christi and fide Christi literally read "faith of [Jesus] Christ" (traditionally taken as objective genitive, "faith in Christ," though also debated as subjective, "faithfulness of Christ"); the Vulgate also uses present-tense credimus ("we believe") rather than the Greek aorist ("we believed").
notes.2:19: In the Clementine Vulgate verse division, Christo confixus sum cruci ("I have been nailed to the cross with Christ") concludes verse 19 rather than beginning verse 20.
notes.3:1: The Clementine Vulgate includes "not to obey the truth" (non obedire veritati) and "among you" (in vobis), phrases absent from many modern Greek critical editions.
notes.3:11: The Vulgate uses the present tense "lives" (vivit) where the Greek text uses a future ("will live"); similarly, in 3:9 the Vulgate reads future "will be blessed" (benedicentur) against Greek present "are blessed."
notes.3:19: The Vulgate reads "was set in place" (posita est) rather than Greek "was added," and uses an active verb "to whom He had promised" (cui promiserat) rather than a passive.
notes.3:22: The Latin genitive in "the faith of Jesus Christ" (fide Jesu Christi) is widely debated and can be understood either as "faith in Jesus Christ" or as "the faithfulness of Jesus Christ."
notes.3:24: Latin paedagogus denotes a household custodian who supervised a minor child. Notably, the Vulgate reads the ablative "in Christ" (in Christo, as also in 3:27) rather than the Greek accusative meaning "until" or "into Christ."
notes.4:7: The Clementine Vulgate reads third-person singular "he is no longer" (jam non est), continuing the image of the heir from 4:1, whereas the Greek text has second-person singular "you are no longer." In 4:6 the Vulgate also reads "into your hearts" (in corda vestra) against critical Greek "our hearts."
notes.4:18: The Vulgate renders this clause as a second-person imperative, "be zealous for what is good" (Bonum autem aemulamini), whereas the Greek text has a passive infinitive ("it is good to be zealously sought").
notes.4:21: The Vulgate reads "have you not read" (non legistis) rather than the Greek verb meaning "do you not hear/listen to."
notes.4:25: The Clementine Vulgate omits the name Hagar here and translates Greek systoichei ("corresponds to") with "is joined to" (conjunctus est).
notes.4:31: The Clementine Vulgate attaches the final relative clause, "by the freedom with which Christ freed us" (qua libertate Christus nos liberavit), to 4:31 rather than beginning 5:1 with it as in most modern editions.
notes.5:1: In the Clementine Vulgate, the clause concerning the freedom with which Christ set us free concludes 4:31, so 5:1 opens directly with "Stand firm." The passive verb contineri literally means "to be held fast" or "confined."
notes.5:9: The Vulgate reads corrumpit ("corrupts," reflecting an early Western reading) where most Greek manuscripts read "leavens."
notes.5:13: The Clementine Vulgate reads per caritatem Spiritus ("through the love of the Spirit"), whereas the standard Greek text reads simply "through love."
notes.5:19: Across 5:19-21 the Clementine Vulgate lists seventeen works of the flesh, including both impudicitia ("indecency") and luxuria ("debauchery") in 5:19 and homicidia ("murders") in 5:21, and uses consequentur ("obtain") rather than "inherit."
notes.5:22: Across 5:22-23 the Clementine Vulgate enumerates twelve fruits of the Spirit, including longanimitas ("forbearance"), modestia ("modesty"), and castitas ("chastity") alongside the nine found in the standard Greek text.
notes.6:1: Vulgate instruite literally means "instruct" or "set in order," rendering the Greek verb katartizo ("restore," "mend"). The Latin also shifts directly from plural ("you who are spiritual") to singular ("examining yourself, so that you too may not be tempted").
notes.6:5: The Vulgate uses the same noun onus ("burden") and verb portare ("bear") in both 6:2 and 6:5, whereas the Greek distinguishes two different nouns for burden and load.
notes.6:8: In the Clementine Vulgate, "For whatever things a man sows, these he will also reap" begins 6:8 rather than ending 6:7, and uses neuter plurals (quae ... haec) along with in carne sua ("in his own flesh") and in spiritu ("in the Spirit").
notes.6:11: Vulgate qualibus litteris literally means "with what kind of letters" (rather than Greek "with what large letters"), and can also denote "what sort of letter."
notes.6:14: Vulgate per quem ("through whom") is unambiguously masculine and therefore refers to Christ (since Latin crux, "cross," is feminine), whereas the Greek relative pronoun could refer to either Christ or the cross.
